<!---
BEFORE YOU OPEN AN ISSUE:
- If you have a question about content, make sure you are looking at the raw .md files which contain the master version of the text and not in the CSV, JSON, XLSX, PDF, DOCX files which are derived from this.
- Please search the issues in case your question has been discussed before.
- Make sure you are looking at the latest edits at: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/tree/master/4.0
- When you reference requirements, please include them as a link, similarly to this:
[6.1.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x14-V6-Cryptography.md#v61-data-classification)

OTHER NOTES:
- Please do not open a pull request without first opening an associated issue.
- Please carry out all discussion in the associated issue only.
-->
Page in question: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x17-V9-Communications.md

What's the intent of this page? I assume to set parameters for protecting network traffic. I wonder whether "Communications" is the clearest title for this; I sort of expect a discussion of "How OWASP discusses issues with the public"

- I suggest changing the title to "Protect Network Traffic" (or maybe "Protecting...")

I think a lot of the content is not needed. I mean, of course we're looking for:

* Best practices
* Modern browsers

Should we mention tool names as examples? I see arguments on both sides:

For: Tool names provide a context for non-native English speakers
Against: Names suggest an endorsement (or an ad)

I'd also like to set this up in "active voice", as that's easier to read. In general, people avoid reading standards docs because they have trouble relating to them. [Active voice](https://developers.google.com/tech-writing/one/active-voice), as described in the Google Technical Writing Course, can help.

Opened at the suggestion of @elarlang , I invite discussion.

comments.body:
Here's a snippet of how I'd change current lines 14-16:

```
V9.1 Client Security

Ensure all client messages are sent over encrypted networks, using TLS 1.2 or later. 
Use up-to-date tools to review the client configuration on a regular basis.
```

Maybe aligning with PCI-DSS Requirement 4 "Encrypt transmission of ~cardholder~ _application_ data ~across open, public networks~" would ensure greater initial community acceptance?

I can ask ISO and Standards Australia what there position is on Active Voice?

Thanks @cmlh . I looked up the ISO "How to Write Standards" [PDF](https://www.iso.org/files/live/sites/isoorg/files/developing_standards/docs/en/how-to-write-standards.pdf), page 3, and I see the following statements on Active Voice and "plain language"

![Screen Shot 2021-10-27 at 1 30 52 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/84352037/139142636-9d9660d7-85ea-4e5b-9001-b42004a90d52.png)

I've drafted some changes (before the tables) for the content, to:

* Push active voice
* Format content where possible in bulleted lists (ref [Google Tech Writing Course guidance](https://developers.google.com/tech-writing/one/lists-and-tables#choose_the_correct_type_of_list)

If y'all like, I'll be happy to push this into a PR:

```
# V9 Communications

## Control Objective

Ensure that a verified application meets the following high level requirements:

* Require TLS or strong encryption, independent of sensitivity of the content.
* Follow the latest guidance, including:
  * Configuration advice
  * Preferred algorithms and ciphers
* Avoid weak or soon to be deprecated algorithms and ciphers, except as a last resort
* Disable deprecated or known insecure algorithms and ciphers.

Within these requirements:

* Stay current with recommended industry advice on secure TLS configuration, as it changes frequently.
* Use the most recent versions of TLS configuration review tools (such as SSLyze or other TLS scanners) to configure the preferred order and algorithm selection.
* Check your configuration periodically to ensure that secure communication is always present and effective.

## V9.1 Client Communications Security

Ensure all client messages are sent over encrypted networks, using TLS 1.2 or later.
Use up-to-date tools to review the client configuration on a regular basis.
```

This is great work but we are right in the middle of a 4.0.3 release. Can you please coordinate with @elarlang before you submit any PR's during this time? Once 4.0.3 is out this will be less of a deal. We are just moving folders around and will have a new working directory soon.

But I really like the direction of your work. We REALLY need _active voice_ for requirements. I am with you!
Thank you @jmanico . I did not know your schedule restrictions. I'll be happy to submit once 4.0.3 is released.
Thank you. I'm looking forward to your PR's and thank you for understanding!

For my taste it was breaking change and not influencing v4.0.3.

Also, the status here is discussion, so it's not in the PR zone yet I think. In general it makes sense to wait till new folder structure is done.
Some of this language actually got included in 4.0.3 but I would certainly suggest waiting for the rest until the updated folder structure is done

@mjang-cobalt [states](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1106#issuecomment-953287770):

> I see the following statements on Active Voice and "plain language"

I'd assume these are one and the same as `plainlanguage.gov` and `use-active-voice` and part of  https://www.plainlanguage.gov/guidelines/conversational/use-active-voice/

LGTM 👍 

Should the Pull Request[s] reference this issue or should @mjang-cobalt break it down into smaller issues for each  requirement for instance?
I see the announcement that 4.0.3 is released, and different suggestions on what to do. To address @elarlang's concerns, what do we need to get this issue to "the PR zone"?

The new working directory is found here:

https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/tree/master/5.0/en

Can you kindly aim your PR's at that directory? Let's do it! If you can lets do several small PR's as opposed to one big one if you are changing a lot of content to active voice. :)

Actually, it looks like @tghosth already merged my suggestions in [this commit](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/commit/ad7d5e055b639e3fff27a9aff3fd92ce5248f39b#diff-bada4aa70302a7407a45a6827a013df4202ebcfba60bb61f39abd00cf6c93f36)

I know some had concerns upthread, so I'm happy to answer specific questions before we close this issue.

(With this change, can I add myself to https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x01-Frontispiece.md#other-contributors-and-reviewers ?)
Since my suggestions are now in ASVS 4.0.3, and @jmanico as merged my PR, I believe we can close this issue.
